title: Constant coefficient tensor comparison
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $T,U$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work on small representatives of their small etale sites in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], in the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(S_{\Et},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $Rj_*$ for the unbounded K-injective derived direct image and $j^{-1}\dashv Rj_*$ for the derived adjunction of [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Suppose that $Rj_*$ preserves countable coproducts. For every $K\in D(U_{\Et},A)$ and every finite $A$-module $N$ (finite as a set, equivalently finitely generated since $A$ is finite), the canonical tensor comparison is an isomorphism:
$$
 (Rj_*K)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_T
 \longrightarrow Rj_*(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N_U).
$$
Here $N_T,N_U$ are the constant module sheaves, placed in degree zero [def-kun-constant-sheaf], the tensors are ordinary uncompleted etale derived tensors [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the displayed morphism is $\mathrm{PF}_j(K,N_T)$ of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] under the canonical identification $j^{-1}N_T\simeq N_U$.

proof.text: Construct the resolution in ModuleCat A explicitly: cover each module M by the free module on its underlying elements, sending e_x to x, and iterate the kernels. The cover is surjective by e_x; kernel inclusion gives the differential and d squared is zero. Exactness follows from surjectivity onto the next kernel, and the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Since A and N are finite, all syzygies and all bases are finite. This imposes no finite-projective-dimension assumption.

proof.text: Let c be the exact derived constant-sheaf functor from D(A) to D(T_et,A). For fixed K let tau be the canonical projection natural transformation, and let alpha be tau precomposed with c. The source library gives the unit normalization isIso_rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap_app_app_tensorUnit and the shift instance commShift_rightDerivedLowerStarProjectionMap_app. Together with the monoidal constant-sheaf unit and singleFunctorObjUnitIso, these show alpha is invertible at A[0]. Both composite functors are triangulated. Working in D(A) avoids a separate identification of the entire pulled-back resolution.

proof.text: For a finite module M, its free module A^(M) is the finite coproduct of copies of A. Use finsuppLEquivDirectSum, ModuleCat.coproductCoconeIsColimit, the derived coproduct cocone, and NatTrans.isIso_app_of_isColimit_cofan. Since triangulated functors are additive, they preserve this finite coproduct. Thus alpha is invertible on each free resolution term in degree zero.

proof.text: For each brutal truncation in degrees -m through 0, apply DerivedCategory.isIso_app_Q_obj_of_isStrictlyGE_of_isStrictlyLE to the preceding termwise isomorphisms. The existing bounded-complex lemma inducts using the distinguished short-exact-sequence triangles and two out of three for a shift-compatible natural transformation.

The brutal truncations form an increasing family whose union is the resolution. Apply the already proved module-complex theorem CochainComplex.telescopeShortComplex_shortExact from ModuleCatTelescope, and DerivedCategory.triangleOfSES_distinguished. Its first two terms are the countable coproduct of the truncations. This proves the required telescope directly in modules before applying c.

The derived constant-sheaf functor preserves countable coproducts through its derived adjunction and leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. Derived inverse image preserves them by derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction. Tensoring preserves them by derivedTensorHomAdjunction, and derived direct image preserves them by the stated hypothesis. Apply NatTrans.isIso_app_of_isColimit_cofan to the countable sum; its component is invertible. Shift compatibility makes alpha a morphism of the image telescope triangles; NatTrans.isIso_app_obj₃_of_isIso_app_obj₁₂ gives invertibility at the resolution.

proof.text: Transfer along the augmentation isomorphism in D(A), using NatTrans.isIso_app_iff_of_iso. Finally Functor.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor identifies c(N[0]) with the constant sheaf N_T in degree zero, and naturality transfers invertibility to the exact component in the statement. The theorem already states the canonical projection map at N_T[0], so no separate pullback-constant-module theorem is needed.
